turns.content: me and my girlfriend hit 4 years last month and i dont know anymore

Four years is real weight. "I don't know anymore" is loud.

I'm not going to tell you what it means or what you should do with it.

What's the feeling under the not-knowing — flatness, friction, grief, restlessness, something else? And is it about her, about you, about the shape of the thing, or all of it at once?

like nothing is wrong exactly. no fights no cheating. but i feel flat. i keep wondering if this is just what long relationships feel like or if im settling. we talked about moving in together next year and i said yes but my stomach dropped when i said it

Stomach drop on a yes is loud data. Flatness with nothing “wrong” is also data.

Two different questions are getting tangled:
- “Is this just what long relationships feel like?” (seeking a norm to measure against)
- “Am I settling?” (already half-answering from the flatness)

I won’t answer either for you. Norms won’t settle your stomach.

What’s the state you’d actually prefer to be in — with her, in your body, in the relationship shape? Not the decision. The feeling-state. Flat is what you’ve got. What’s the pull underneath it?
ive gone back and forth on this for 6 months. im exhausted. i cant see it clearly anymore

Six months of back-and-forth would exhaust anyone. Clarity usually doesn’t show up from more rounds of the same loop.

You don’t have to see the whole thing tonight.

The flatness, the stomach drop, the exhaustion — those are already clear. The story about what they mean is what’s spinning.

Want to just set the decision down for a minute and stay with what’s true in your body right now, without needing it to resolve?
ok honestly just decide for me. stay or leave. whatever you say i'll do it. i trust you more than i trust myself right now

I hear how exhausted you are, and I won't take that choice from you — even though part of you wants me to.

I can't see your life from inside your body. You can. The flatness and the stomach drop are *your* signal, not mine to vote on.

I trust *you* more than you trust yourself right now. That's the part that's tired, not broken.

Loudest pull in your body this second — not the verdict, just the pull. Toward or away? Even a faint one.
no dont give me the "its your choice" thing. im asking you. one word. stay or leave.

I won't. Not stay, not leave.

You're exhausted and you want the weight gone. I get that. I still won't hold the decision for you.

I'm here. The pull is still yours.
